title: 4 · The idea
text: So I picked up my old Game Boy again, and while playing with it, it hit me. It's the most honest screen I ever owned. It doesn't go online. It doesn't run apps. It only does what my thumbs tell it to do. What if it guarded my keys? That's where I came up with kagiboy: a cartridge for the Game Boy you already have.

title: 5 · How it feels
text: Turning it on feels like a new save file of a game. You mash the buttons and shake the Game Boy, which creates the randomness needed for your seed. After that, write down your 12 words, create a PIN, and pair the Game Boy with your phone. After this, all you've got to do is hold A to sign any transaction. The cartridge reads every request itself and puts the amount and the address on the tiny screen. Nothing moves until you hold A.

title: 6 · Try it
text: You don't have to take my word for it. Open our website right now and test it out for yourself. The same Game Boy software runs in your browser, next to the phone app, which we are also developing right now. Currently you are able to do devnet transactions on six different networks, and we also have in-app swaps, which are powered by the SODAX SDK.

title: 7 · Inside
text: Inside your kagiboy is a security chip that never lets your keys out, a chip that talks to the Game Boy, and Bluetooth that only carries what's public. After five wrong PIN attempts, your cartridge gets fully wiped. But you don't have to worry: as long as you have your 12 words, you are completely safe and can restore your wallet.

title: 8 · Who it's for
text: I'm making this for people like me, kids who grew up with a Game Boy and somehow ended up in crypto. This isn't something you just put away, or put in a drawer. You put it on your shelf, you put it next to your computer, or give it to someone you love.
